page: UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-960GB-4xH100 is a GPU-accelerated server designed for high-density compute and memory-intensive workloads. It features 48 physical cores powered by Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processors running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 960 GB of system memory, providing 20 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is driven by four NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs, delivering a combined 320 GB of VRAM.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in memory bandwidth and data decompression. The system achieved a read-only small block memory bandwidth of 7,649.82 GB/sec and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 615.79 GB/sec. CPU capabilities are highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 85,426.66 and an extended instructions test score of 117,918.35, supported by hardware-level Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512. For language model tasks, the server demonstrated prompt processing speeds of 10,308.98 tokens/sec on a small 135M model.

This server class offers high resource density, combining massive GPU memory with substantial system RAM, which is qualitatively cost-efficient for large-scale parallel processing. However, users must note certain architectural tradeoffs. The CPU resources are allocated on a shared basis, and the instance does not include any local storage, requiring external storage solutions for data persistence.

Given the four NVIDIA H100 GPUs and 960 GB of RAM, this server is suited for large-scale artificial intelligence workloads, including LLM training, high-throughput inference, and deep learning. The presence of Intel AMX and AVX-512 instructions also makes it appropriate for scientific simulations, heavy cryptography, and complex data decompression pipelines.
description: The UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-960GB-4xH100 is a high-density GPU-accelerated server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 48 Intel Xeon 8462Y+ physical cores running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 960 GB of system memory and four NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs providing 320 GB of total VRAM. Designed for parallel computing, it delivers top-tier performance in memory bandwidth and multi-threaded decompression, alongside strong PassMark CPU scores supported by Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512. Tradeoffs include a shared CPU allocation and the absence of local storage. This configuration is highly suited for deep learning, large language model inference, and intensive scientific simulations.
